evidence.text: Do Treasury Yields Mean for Investors? By Adam Carpenter | Updated: Dec. 7, 2023 | By Adam Carpenter | Updated: Dec. 7, 2023 Save ...more Table of Contents What Are Treasury Yields? How Do Treasury Yields Work? Yield Curve More What Are Treasury Yields? A Treasury yield refers to the effective yearly interest rate the U.S. government pays on money it borrows to raise capital through selling Treasury bonds , also referred to as Treasury notes or Treasury bills depending on maturity length. Long-term bond yields are also indicators of investor confidence in the U.S. economy, and when Treasury bonds have low yields, people tend to look to stocks and other investments for better returns. Related: Sign up for stock news with our Invested newsletter. How Do Treasury Yields Work? The driving principle behind treasury yields is demand. In other words, the higher the demand for treasury bonds, the lower the yield and vice versa. Yields drop when demand is high and rise when demand is low.

could get pricier There is also a correlation between Treasury yields and student loans . A college education is the second-largest expense an individual is likely to face in a lifetime, right after purchasing a home. To cover that cost, more than half of families borrow . Undergraduate students who take out new direct federal student loans for the 2023-24 academic year are now paying 5.50% — up from 4.99% in the 2022-23 academic year and 3.73% in 2021-22. The government sets the annual rates on those loans once a year, based on the 10-year Treasury . If the 10-year yield stays above 5%, federal student loan interest rates could increase again when they reset in the spring, costing student borrowers even more in interest. Car loans are getting more expensive There is also a loose correlation between Treasury yields and auto loans . The average rate on a five-year new car loan is currently 7.62%, the highest in 16 years, according to Bankrate. Now, more consumers face monthly payments

does not always guarantee a recession, however. Are Treasury yields and Treasury bonds the same thing? No. A Treasury yield is the effective annual interest rate paid by the U.S. government to a bondholder. A Treasury bond is a loan that you make to the government. What does a high Treasury yield mean? Higher long-term yields mean that demand for Treasury bonds is decreasing, which indicates that investors are looking elsewhere for better returns.
